findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility could use some deep cleaning. Floors throughout the facility were observed with general debris in the walk in cooler, behind the counter, and the storage areas. Can rings, card board boxes, empty soda cans, and various waste products that appear to have been incorrectly discarded were observed on the floors of the facility. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained in a manner that prevents debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Shelving and slides used for drink storage in coolers remain to be cleaned. Owner ordered new slides. Shelving will be cleaned and sliders will be replaced once new ones arrive. Maintain shelving and new slides clean.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.12 Floor remains to be cleaned in the following areas:
1) in the middle of the store under shelves used for food and alcohol storage; and
2) in the walk-in cooler under shelving and along the wall beneath the reach-in doors.
Ensure floors under shelving and in the walk-in cooler are cleaned as needed.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B), & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Multiple priority violations were observed during inspection today. Also, facility was observed operating as a Class II medium risk establishment at the time of inspection and is permitted as a Class III low risk establishment. See additional violations for details. Follow-up inspection will be conducted to revisit active managerial controls and revisit operations.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Ice was packaged on-site to sell for the purpose of consumption in styrofoam cups with lids. Adequate facilities are not currently present to allow for this practice (see #10), and hands could not have been properly washed prior to packaging due to lack of handwashing sink in the area where product was packaged. Cease the practice of packaging ice on-site in cups for purchase. This practice may only resume if store is remodeled to allow for install of proper facilities.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles and prior to putting on gloves to handle food.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing sign was not posted in the employee restroom. Handwashing sign was provided. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-204.11 Facility is not adequately equipped with a handwashing sink in the front of the store where ice was handled to prepare cups for individual sale. Owner confirmed the retail freezer was used as food handling area prior to storage of cups in the freezer. A handwashing sink must be provided if owner wishes to sell ice packaged on-site. The handwashing sink in the employee restroom does not suffice for the purposes of handwashing prior to food handling. Cease the practice of packaging ice on-site in cups for purchase. This practice may only resume if store is remodeled to allow for install of proper facilities.
Handwashing sinks shall be located to allow convenient use by employees in food preparation, food dispensing, and ware washing areas.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 Styrofoam cups with ice were observed in a small freezer available for purchase. The facility is a Class III low risk establishment and does not have proper facilities to allow for retail sale of ice packaged on-site for the purpose of consumption. All cups of ice and open bag of partially used ice observed in retail freezer were dumped on the ground outside the facility to dispose of the ice during inspection. Cease the practice of packaging ice on-site for the purposes of consumption. Class II medium risk permit and adequate facilities are required to allow for this practice. Ice chest outside the facility was observed and confirmed to contain only packaged ice from approved source (Home City Ice).
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice scoop used to portion bagged ice into cups is unable to be properly cleaned due to lack of adequate facilities (see #48). Cease the practice of using the ice scoop for packaging ice to be sold for the purposes of consumption. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be cleaned at least up to every 24hrs or more frequently any time when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Ice scoop is unable to be properly sanitized due to lack of adequate facilities (#48). Cease the practice of using the ice scoop for packaging ice to be sold for the purposes of consumption.
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Retail ice cream freezer was observed with heavy ice buildup inside. Defrost and clean the freezer as needed to allow for ease in cleaning. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-301.12 Facility is not adequately equipped with a 3 compartment sink to allow for manual wash, rinse, and sanitize of ice scoop. A 3 part sink with compartments large enough for immersion of equipment and utensils must be provided if owner wishes to sell ice packaged on-site. 
A sink with at least 3 compartments shall be provided for manually washing, rinsing, and sanitizing equipment and utensils. Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of here largest equipment and utensils.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1) Shelving and plastic organizers used for beverages in the walk-in cooler were soiled with mold and general debris accumulation. Shelving in need of cleaning were closest to the walk-in cooler entrance.
2) Shelving and plastic organizers in drink coolers were soiled with mold buildup, especially coolers by the front door.
3) Tracks to sliding door cooler by front door were soiled with dirt and debris.
Ensure cleaning of general surfaces as needed, including inside coolers.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Observed the ice cream freezer to have a large build up of frost/ice, which makes the ice machine not smooth or easily cleanable. Ensure the frost is removed from the freezer. 
(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
